items.summary: Agent prefix-cache misses are usually caused by non-deterministic prompt serialization like shuffled tool-schema keys, and fixing serialization plus prompt layout took cache hits from 55% to 95% and first-token latency from ~27s to 7.3s.
items.rating_reason: Exceptional firsthand LLM-inference engineering: the author measures prefix-cache hit rates before and after tuning, traces mysterious cache misses by tokenizing and diffing consecutive prompts, and root-causes a subtle bug where Go map randomization in the MCP gateway shuffled tool-schema key order, invalidating 100k+ cached tokens per turn, with merged upstream fixes and a Jinja workaround. It also documents non-obvious hybrid-attention cache behavior (2048-token block boundaries that make CPU KV offload nearly useless) and a practical, evidence-backed checklist including the finding that speculative decoding's verdict flips once the cache is warm. Relevance to the reader's LLM-systems and agent-engineering interests is direct, and the density of measurements, configs, and reproducible debugging steps is very high. The main limitation is that some findings are specific to Qwen3.8-27B, vLLM 0.28.0, and the oh-my-pi/Bifrost stack, though the methodology generalizes.

items.title: AI watermarking has a decentralisation problem
items.summary: AI watermarking must be globally coordinated to let users reliably detect any AI‑generated content, but fragmented key usage and defection incentives make such coordination extremely difficult.
items.rating_reason: The article delivers concrete technical details about watermarking mechanisms (e.g., SynthID keyed token selection), shows how key governance creates a decentralization challenge, and explains incentives for defection and coordination failures. It provides original evidence and mechanisms relevant to AI policy and inference ecosystems, though it contains modest promotional padding.

items.title: What I Measured After Hacker News Broke My LLM Agent Gate
items.summary: A careful, reproducible measurement of a provenance-based LLM agent gate shows it reduces attack success from 97% to 9% but at meaningful utility cost, while text-pattern detection fundamentally cannot see the majority of real attacks whose harm is policy conflict, not phrasing.
items.rating_reason: Exceptional measurement-driven account of prompt-injection defense for LLM agents. The author isolates the capability gate's effect from model behavior via a replay harness, reports specific numbers across five iterative improvements, and provides genuinely non-obvious findings: 59% of real attacks carry no textual marker (the attack is policy conflict, not phrasing), provenance-based gating cuts attack success from 97% to 9% at a real utility cost, and current capable models refused every tested injection on their own. Honesty about limitations (benchmark distortions, single-deployment policy, unmeasured real-world utility) and the reproducible harness elevate this above typical security blog content.

items.title: The Capacity Paradox
items.summary: Adding engineers can actually degrade validated‑feature output when the evaluation gate is too loose, and diagnosing queue dynamics reveals the true bottleneck.
items.rating_reason: The article presents a concrete, well‑engineered Petri‑net model that quantifies the hidden cost of adding engineers, shows diagnostic evidence that a tight evaluation gate improves outcomes, and demonstrates a general diagnostic method applicable across unrelated systems. Its insights are technically deep and substantively different from typical spreadsheets, yet it relies on specialized tooling that most readers may not have immediate access to, limiting universal applicability.

items.title: Device Bound Session Credentials in ASP.NET Core
items.summary: DBSC ties sessions to device‑bound private keys, requiring cryptographic proof to refresh and greatly reducing replay viability.
items.rating_reason: Provides concrete, well‑described mechanisms for tying sessions to device‑bound private keys, including key generation, registration, challenge signing, storage in encrypted refresh cookies, and trade‑offs of short‑lived cookie expiration; experimental, limited browser support.

items.title: How to Run a Two-Tier Offline CA
items.summary: You can construct a cost‑effective, air‑gapped two‑tier CA on Raspberry Pis with hardened images, split‑personality ceremonies, and strict name‑constraint policies.
items.rating_reason: The article delivers a concrete, step‑by‑step guide for building a two‑tier offline CA on Raspberry Pi hardware, including exact commands, image‑hardening procedures, and ceremony scripts. It provides practical security mechanisms (name constraints, pathlen=0, split passphrase, hardware token protection) and a clear maintenance schedule, making it highly actionable for engineers. While the concept of an offline CA is not novel, the depth of implementation detail and reproducible instructions give it strong value for a technically capable audience.

items.title: <![CDATA[Pluggable, Extensible, and Playful DevTools]]>
items.summary: Devframe provides one stable definition and Web Standard handler that can be mounted in any framework‑agnostic host, enabling modular, composable DevTools shared across ecosystems.
items.rating_reason: The article presents a concrete, framework‑neutral definition for DevTools, complete with code snippets, adapter patterns, and real‑world plugin examples. It delivers non‑obvious technical insight and measurable mechanisms for reusing DevTool functionality across hosts, which directly serves engineers seeking deeper tooling capabilities. The content is dense with implementation details, but occasional promotional phrasing prevents a perfect score.

items.title: Signed Tags as a Release Gate
items.summary: SSH-signed tags enforced via pre-receive hooks and verify-before-deploy scripts create a release authorization gate that is independent of third-party platform protections, with several subtle implementation details that matter for correctness.
items.rating_reason: Substantive, well-tested article on using SSH-signed git tags as a release authorization gate. It provides reproducible commands and scripts, documents non-obvious gotchas (verifying by SHA not ref name in pre-receive hooks because refs don't exist yet, distinguishing 'Good signature' from trusted signature via allowed_signers), and is honest about limitations (key custody, no correctness guarantee, no review timing). The technical depth is strong without padding.

items.title: Hacking the Millennium Problem Is Not Solving Turbulence
items.summary: AI can solve a formal breakdown case by retro‑fitting a force, but this does not address the physical turbulence problem, which the author tackles with a stable statistical framework tied to Riemann zeros.
items.rating_reason: The post delivers concrete, technically dense analysis of how an AI-generated breakthrough on a Navier–Stokes Millennium case merely manufactures a force to force a singular velocity field, exposing the loophole and highlighting the lack of stability. It then outlines a substantive, original candidate solution to true turbulence that links statistical laws to Riemann zeros and proves Lyapunov stability, providing measurable insight beyond hype. The main limitation is its reliance on a dense mathematical narrative without raw data or reproducible code, which may impede quick comprehension for some readers.

items.title: Jump to main content
items.summary: SparroWocky is a sophisticated Salt Typhoon backdoor targeting Latin American entities, using open‑source tools and advanced evasion to support China’s strategic monitoring of US influence.
items.rating_reason: The article provides several genuine value instances: novel intel on the SparroWocky backdoor, detailed technical breakdown of its components and evasion methods, geopolitical analysis of its target shift, and links to IOCs on ESET's GitHub. It stays on topic, offers actionable insight for security professionals, and contains no clickbait or padding, yielding a high value density for a medium‑length piece.

items.title: #1 Trusted Cybersecurity News Platform
items.summary: Anyone running Unbound should upgrade to 1.26.1 or apply patches immediately, since a critical DNSSEC validator heap overflow reachable via a malicious zone enables possible remote code execution on every prior release.
items.rating_reason: The core article is dense, timely security reporting with high actionable value for DNS operators: a critical RCE-capable heap overflow in Unbound's DNSSEC validator (CVE-2026-81642) affecting all versions through 1.26.0, eight additional CVEs itemized in a table with trigger conditions and impacts, concrete remediation steps (upgrade to 1.26.1 or apply patch -p1 commands), Debian branch patch status, the val-clean-additional default change, and useful context distinguishing the maintainer's 9.1 CVSS from NVD's pending analysis. The article adds genuine value beyond a press release by clarifying exploitation status, attribution, and patch applicability. Heavy site boilerplate (navigation, promoted webinars, related-story lists) inflates length without adding value, which slightly dilutes density. Thematic relevance is strong for CyberSecurity and Sysadmin audiences running DNS infrastructure.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra crushes Pokemon, Factorio, and Fallout 3 then spirals into Minecraft potato farming after one bad Creeper
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents can turn raw gameplay experience into reusable symbolic rules, but single failures may imprint overly rigid habits.
items.rating_reason: The article provides concrete performance data showing GPT‑6 Astra’s breakthroughs across multiple games, explains the novel "check‑first‑then‑repeat" rule‑learning method, and highlights both its strengths and the risk of over‑correction—offering genuine insights into autonomous AI agents. Minor click‑bait in the title slightly detracts, but overall value density is solid for a medium‑length piece.

items.title: The Brutal Reality For Most Men Today (& how to fix it) - Dr K HealthyGamer
items.summary: Men use porn, gambling, and gaming as compulsive coping mechanisms for meaninglessness, and understanding this cycle reveals pathways to address these behaviors.
items.rating_reason: The piece delivers multiple novel insights—such as the addiction cycle, video games as evolutionary substitutes, and purpose as a protective factor—while aligning tightly with human development and psychology themes. The brief promotional intro is minor padding but does not diminish the substantive value. Overall the content offers high value density and strong thematic relevance.

items.title: AWS EKS forensics: data sources and investigation tooling
items.summary: Integrating AWS logging services enables efficient detection and investigation of Kubernetes attacks in EKS.
items.rating_reason: The piece delivers multiple concrete forensic techniques for EKS, such as layered data source mapping and specific CloudWatch Insights queries, providing actionable value for security practitioners. It stays focused, avoids fluff, and aligns well with CyberSecurity and Tech themes, earning a strong but not exceptional score.
